metadata.description: Skills for AI agents, made and tested by MBSI. Each one is a plain folder you can read before you install it.

plugins.name: be-ambitious
plugins.description: Before your agent starts, it asks what the job is really for and what an expert would do, then asks for more than you first typed.

plugins.name: but-therefore
plugins.description: Rebuilds a devlog or post as a chain of "but" and "therefore" instead of "and then".

plugins.name: cognitive-prophylactics
plugins.description: Before you draft, it asks for one line: the situation your reader might meet and the move that lifts or lowers their standing in it.

plugins.name: decide
plugins.description: It compares the options for each person a choice affects, including doing nothing, then shows you a short result you can check.

plugins.name: dig-apc
plugins.description: After a failure, it has your agent write what it did and what it believed, as axioms, principles and cruxes, then test each belief to find the one that is wrong.

plugins.name: encode-lessons
plugins.description: When the same correction comes up a second time, it picks the cheapest guard that holds it (a type, a lint rule, a hook or a script) instead of adding another line of text.

plugins.name: first-principles
plugins.description: When a rule changes, it redesigns the type model or module from the start instead of adding another special case.

plugins.name: lever
plugins.description: When the work isn't trivial, it has your agent write the script that does it, rerun it on the first unit and diff the result against the hand version.

plugins.name: prove-it
plugins.description: Before your agent says it is done, it runs the real program from outside and reads what it prints, instead of trusting a compile, a cached screenshot or its own word.

plugins.name: signal-chain
plugins.description: It ranks ways of carrying a message by how costly each is for the reader to decode, from faces and voices to writing and symbols, so you choose the one they can afford.

plugins.name: skill-design
plugins.description: A change to a skill, rule or hook ships only if it is small, one or two intentful edits, because every added line carries claims nobody checked.

plugins.name: unblock
plugins.description: Your agent proceeds on reversible work, settles the mechanics itself and shows what it did and why, and still asks first about anything hard to reverse, outward-facing or costly.

plugins.name: why-this-piece
plugins.description: Before you write, it asks four questions in writing: the point of the piece, why a reader would care, the business goal, and what making it says about us.
